newsitem.title: USA: Twisters, thunderstorms spare Texas refineries.
newsitem.headline: Twisters, thunderstorms spare Texas refineries.

text.p: There were no immediate reports of significant damage to oil refineries in the Houston area after tornadoes and thunderstorms swept through the refinery-studded region earlier Tuesday afternoon.

A storm reportedly spawned at least three funnel clouds as it moved through Harris County toward the southeast and the Gulf Coast, leaving an estimated 234,000 Houston Lighting and Power Co customers without electicity in the Houston area.
Police in nearby Pasadena, Texas, reported sightings of two twisters in the town which is home to numerous refineries, including the 100,000-barrel-per day (bpd) Crown Central Petroleum Corp plant.

"They tore down limbs and downed power lines," said Police Officer D.K. Bell. But he added the twisters touched down on the west side of town, three miles away from the town's Northside corridor of refineries.
Shell Oil Co said workers at its Houston Headquarters had to leave their posts to move to the center of the building as the tornadoes came through town.
However, a Shell spokesperson said its 255,700 bpd Deer Park refinery was not affected by power outages caused by severe storms.
A Valero Refining Co spokeperson said its 125,4000 bpd Texas City refinery (formerly owned by Basis Petroleum) had reported no problems.
Marathon Oil Co said operations continued to run smoothly at its 70,000 barrel per day Texas City, Texas, refinery. "There are no problems," said spokesman Bill Ryder.
The Community Awareness Emergency Response (CAER), which monitors refinery trouble along "refinery row" in the Gulf, said it had not had reports of refinery outages in the wake of the storms.
